sections.html:
Albemarle County is in the Virginia Piedmont and covers about 726 square miles. It wraps around the independent city of Charlottesville, borders eight other counties, more than any other county in the state, and runs west into Shenandoah National Park. Scottsville is the largest incorporated town. Crozet, North Garden, Earlysville, Stony Point, Ivy, Pantops, Hollymead and Monticello show up often in addresses and fire station names.

The 2020 census counted 112,395 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 118,356. Charlottesville is a separate government, and the county seat sits inside it even though the land around it is Albemarle County. Each bills its own property tax. The county's GIS-Web viewer shows assessment data and is the place to confirm that your parcel is in the county before you look up a bill.

The county's comprehensive plan steers new development into Development Areas, which make up about 5 percent of the county. The rest is Rural Area meant for agriculture, natural resource protection and some homes. The Board of Supervisors adopted the current plan, AC44, on October 15, 2025.

Assessment reports sort property the same way: urban residential on county water and sewer, residential up to 20 acres, and rural parcels of 20 to 99.99 acres and of 100 acres or more. Knowing which group your house falls in tells you which line of the reassessment table applies to you.

The county's total tax base rose 6.17 percent in 2026, driven by continued appreciation in residential values. Staff review about 20 percent of properties in detail each year, and in 2026 they reviewed more than 16,000. First-half bills mailed in May use the new value and the rate set in April.

Property type2026 change in assessed value
Urban residential (county water and sewer)+5.4%
Residential up to 20 acres+8.1%
Rural, 20 to 99.99 acres+7.5%
Rural, 100 acres and over+7.1%
Multi-family+4.6%
Commercial+3.0%

By magisterial district the average change ran from +3.6% in Rivanna to +9.8% in Samuel Miller, and the Town of Scottsville averaged +4.1%. Neighborhoods move at different rates, so your own notice can differ widely from these averages.

Albemarle has two appeal steps: an administrative review first, then a Board of Equalization appeal. The calendar shifts a little each year, but the pattern holds.

  • Assessment notices are mailed in late January, with the data online in the county GIS the next day.
  • The Administrative Review form is due in early March.
  • The Board of Equalization application is due at the end of March, or 30 days after an Administrative Review result, whichever is later.
  • First-half bills go out in May, based on the new value and the rate the Board of Supervisors sets in April.

Call the Assessor's Office at 434-296-5856 before you file anything. Virginia requires real estate to be assessed at 100 percent of fair market value under Va. Code 58.1-3201, so your argument is about value, not the rate.

The county's tax rates page lists a real estate rate of $0.894 per $100 of assessed value for residential, commercial and land. To estimate a bill, divide the assessed value by 100 and multiply by the rate. The rate is set each April, and the first-half bill in May uses it. Confirm the current year with the Finance Department.

The same page lists a 1 percent daily short-term rental tax and a 9 percent transient occupancy tax, effective July 1, 2024. If you rent a house short term, bring those accounts current before a sale.

The county offers real estate tax relief for certain elderly and permanently disabled owners, and a land use program that defers tax on qualifying farm and forest land.

  • Relief: the owner of record must be at least 65 or certified totally and permanently disabled. In the 2024 program year, combined income could be no more than $88,800 and net worth no more than $305,000. Finance can give the current limits at 434-296-5852.
  • Land use: applications are due January 1. Owners whose notice showed an increase, or who held a newly created parcel, can apply for a short time afterward with a $125 non-refundable fee per parcel.

If you sell land in the program, ask the Assessor's Office what happens to the deferral before you close.

Virginia charges a state recordation tax of 25 cents per $100 on a deed under Va. Code 58.1-801, applied to the greater of the price or the most recent assessment. A grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500 under 58.1-802 falls on the seller as grantor. Local recordation and other fees are set separately, so ask the title company for a full statement.

sections.h2: Planning a sale around the tax calendar
sections.html:
Timing matters in Albemarle because the value on your January notice drives the first-half bill in May. If you plan to list in spring, read the notice the week it arrives. A value that looks high gives you only a short window to ask for an administrative review before the Board of Equalization deadline, and a lower assessed value also gives a buyer a more reasonable tax figure to plan around.

Acreage owners should look at which group their parcel belongs to. A residential lot up to 20 acres rose 8.1 percent in 2026, while rural parcels of 20 to 99.99 acres rose 7.5 percent and those of 100 acres or more rose 7.1 percent. Parcels on county water and sewer rose 5.4 percent. If your own change is far from the group figure, that is a reason to call the Assessor before you file.

A seller with an unpaid Albemarle bill can still sell. The title company pays the balance from proceeds. Ask for a payoff that includes penalty and interest, and check that the second-half bill is covered if closing falls near its due date.

Call the Finance Department at 434-296-5852 for the bill and the Assessor's Office at 434-296-5856 for value questions. This is general information, and a Virginia attorney can advise on your title.

Gather the latest bill, the assessment notice and any short-term rental tax account before you list. If an inherited or rental house has fallen behind on tax and repairs, we buy houses as-is and can build the closing around the payoff, so the balance is settled at the table and you see the figure first.

faqs.q: Is Charlottesville part of Albemarle County?
faqs.a: No. Charlottesville is an independent city entirely surrounded by Albemarle County, and the county seat is located there. Each government bills its own property tax.

faqs.q: What was the 2026 Albemarle County reassessment?
faqs.a: The county's total tax base rose 6.17 percent, with residential property up 5.4 to 8.1 percent depending on type. Notices went out in January.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Albemarle County assessment?
faqs.a: File the Administrative Review form in early March, then apply to the Board of Equalization by the end of March or 30 days after the review result, whichever is later. Call the Assessor at 434-296-5856 first.

faqs.q: What is the Albemarle County real estate tax rate?
faqs.a: The county tax rates page lists $0.894 per $100 of assessed value. Confirm the current year with the Finance Department.

faqs.q: Who qualifies for Albemarle County elderly tax relief?
faqs.a: In the 2024 program year, owners had to be 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled, with income of no more than $88,800 and net worth of no more than $305,000. Call Finance at 434-296-5852 for current limits.
